column4: Dialect-arm SUBTEST population, one line for the whole shape rather than one per test: this job runs the full unfiltered ./engine/... ./migration/... sweep with ONLY CLEAT_TEST_MYSQL set, so every test with a per-dialect t.Run("postgres", ...) skips that arm here. Measured on a real CI run (cleat#2444, PR #2686, run 36617238081, job 109573287782): `grep '"Action":"skip"' test-report.json | grep -o '"Test":"[^"]*"' | grep -c '/postgres$'` = 405. Bumped to 406 for cleat#2228's TestCleanupTestDataClearsTenantScopedFixtureTables/postgres, which matches this bare suffix pattern too -- check-skip-budget.sh checks each line independently, so a new test's arm counts against BOTH its own named line and any broader suffix line it also matches; the checker cannot distinguish that from something genuinely undeclared. Filed as cleat#2729; this is the workaround, not the fix, and it edits a count this design was meant to keep out of any one PR's way. Measured again for cleat#1980: the real count on develop (d5d85353, before this PR) was already 407, one more than the 406 recorded here -- an unrelated drift this PR did not cause but had to correct to land a true number. cleat#1980 adds TestEntryPointSchemasRoundTrip/postgres and TestEntryPointSchemasNullWhenNotSupplied/postgres (both registeredBackends-style), +2 more. After rebasing onto develop, cleat#1986's own new test (TestAWorkflowDefDefaultsToTheAuthExposureClass) turned out to have independently bumped this same broad line by +1 already (406 -> 407, landed before this PR branched from a fresh develop), so the two bumps combine rather than either superseding the other -- not obvious from the ledger text alone, which is exactly the "checked each line independently" risk this file's own guidance warns about. Re-measured directly rather than added arithmetically: a clean mysql-only run (0 test or package failures, run against a freshly recreated container after an earlier attempt hit residue from container reuse) gives check-skip-budget.sh's own authoritative "got 409" -- the number recorded here.

Same shape as the /postgres$ line above, for the mssql arm of the same dialect-parameterised tests. Measured on the same CI run: 405 -- equal by construction, since the suite parameterises these tests over the SAME set of non-MySQL dialects. Bumped to 406 for the same test's /mssql arm; see the /postgres$ line above for why. Measured again for cleat#1980: the base count (d5d85353) agreed with the recorded 406 here (unlike the /postgres$ line, no pre-existing drift against that base). After rebasing onto develop, the same cleat#1986 bump described on the /postgres$ line above applies here too (406 -> 407), so cleat#1980's +2 combines with it rather than replacing it. Re-measured directly (not added arithmetically) against a clean mysql-only run: check-skip-budget.sh's own "got 409" is the number recorded here.

cleat#2705: names every test in what was previously the bare __UNATTRIBUTED__ remainder, so a SUBSTITUTION inside it (one test stops skipping while a different one starts, netting to the same count) is caught -- the gap cleat-review's #2686 review identified: the remainder was a ceiling with no own-dialect arm, so it already caught #2444's failure mode, but not one test's skip being replaced by a different test's skip at the same total. Names 324 whole tests with no per-dialect subtest split (testutil.TestDB(t, DialectPostgres) or DialectMSSQL called directly), which this job's single MySQL DSN cannot satisfy either way -- same population the old __UNATTRIBUTED__ line described, enumerated instead of counted. Measured on run 36799321585, job 110169881893 (develop HEAD 3f08fd89, 2026-10-01): replicated check-skip-budget.sh's own attribution algorithm exactly (specific named lines removed from the skip-name pool first, then broad suffix lines, most-specific-first, matching the script's own pool-reduction order) rather than a plain name count, since several of this job's skips are already claimed by their own dedicated ledger lines elsewhere (e.g. test-areclaimwindowpast24daysdoesnotoverflow, the-mssql-snapshot-sees-the-attributes-it-selects.tsv) and a naive total-minus-two-suffixes count overlapped them: 333 names matched neither /postgres$ nor /mssql$ directly, but 9 of those are already named elsewhere, leaving exactly 324 -- matching this line's inherited budget exactly, with zero mismatches on every other ledger line for this job (specific or broad) against the same run. May only shrink: as a remaining name here gets dialect-parameterised and its own named line, delete it from this alternation and lower the count by one.

Dialect-arm subtest population, same reasoning as multi-db/mysql's line above: this job sets ONLY CLEAT_TEST_MSSQL, so every dialect-parameterised test's postgres arm skips. Measured on the same CI run (job 109573287789): 405. Bumped to 406 for cleat#2228's TestCleanupTestDataClearsTenantScopedFixtureTables/postgres -- see the multi-db/mysql /postgres$ line's note above (cleat#2729) for why a new test's own named line does not avoid this. cleat#1980 adds TestEntryPointSchemasRoundTrip/postgres and TestEntryPointSchemasNullWhenNotSupplied/postgres (both registeredBackends-style, same mechanism as multi-db/mysql's /postgres$ line above), +2. The full-suite baseline could not be re-measured cleanly on local infrastructure for this bump: the whole mssql-only ./engine/... ./migration/... sweep hit a 10-20 minute test timeout on THREE separate attempts, in three different tests each time (TestTenantIsolation_Signals/mssql, TestMSSQLTenantScopedTablesAreQueriedWithATenantPredicate, and -- on the UNMODIFIED base commit, ruling out this PR as the cause -- TestNoStoreMethodIsReachableOnlyThroughDeadCode), consistent with local QEMU-emulated SQL Server degrading under a long sustained run rather than any one test being broken. After rebasing onto develop, cleat#1986's own new test independently bumped this same broad line by +1 first (406 -> 407, same mechanism confirmed and tool-verified on multi-db/mysql's /postgres$ line, where the combined total came to 409 against a clean re-measurement rather than 408 from arithmetic alone), so this line's count is the SAME combination (407 + cleat#1980's +2 = 409), not re-measured directly here for the local-infrastructure reason above -- worth re-deriving from a real CI run if this drifts again.

Same shape, for the mysql arm. Measured on the same CI run: 402 -- close to but not identical to the postgres count above (405), because the two arm sets are not drawn from exactly the same test population (a test can be parameterised over {postgres, mssql} without a mysql arm, or vice versa). Bumped to 403 for the same test's /mysql arm; same reason as the /postgres$ line above. cleat#1980 adds the same two tests' /mysql arms, +2. Same combination as the /postgres$ line above: cleat#1986's independent +1 (403 -> 404) landed on develop first, so the total is 404 + 2 = 406, not re-measured directly here for the same local-infrastructure reason.
